purpose: Frozen development set (devpl) for the Buffett Partnership letters, built only from partnership letter years 1957, 1960, 1961, 1964, 1967 and 1970. Curated from the frozen corpus without running any retriever or model.

cases.query: Why did Buffett choose the Dow as the benchmark for his partnerships, how long a test did he consider fair, and why did he insist on setting the yardstick in advance?

gold_claims.claim: He chose the Dow because it has the advantage of being widely known and has a long period of continuity, reflecting the experience of investors generally.
gold_claims.verification_note: bpl1961_p0006: terms verbatim in passage text; unit=qualitative statement.

gold_claims.claim: He felt that three years is a very minimal test of performance, ideally judged where the terminal level of the Dow is reasonably close to its initial level.
required_terms: three years is a very minimal test
gold_claims.verification_note: bpl1961_p0006: terms verbatim in passage text; unit=qualitative statement.

gold_claims.claim: He insists on establishing yardsticks prior to the act, since retrospectively, almost anything can be made to look good.
gold_claims.verification_note: bpl1961_p0005: terms verbatim in passage text; unit=qualitative statement.

cases.verification_note: bpl1961_p0006, bpl1961_p0005 supply the 3 claims (widely known; three years is a very minimal test; yardsticks prior to the act).

history.content: What does Buffett think of callable tax-free bonds?
He dislikes them, because the issuer can retire the bond early whenever that suits the issuer and not the buyer.

cases.query: How can an investor avoid that problem, which bond did he single out as a bad example, and how recently had such a bond been sold?

gold_claims.claim: One way to avoid the problem is to buy bonds which are totally noncallable, or discount bonds where the call price is far above your cost.
gold_claims.verification_note: bpl1970_p0030: terms verbatim in passage text; unit=qualitative statement.

history.content: What does Buffett mean by a work-out in his 1957 letter?
An investment whose profit depends on a specific corporate action, such as a sale, merger, liquidation or tender, rather than on a general rise in the stock price.

cases.query: What risk do they carry, how did the mix against general issues shift over the year, and what caused the shift?

gold_claims.claim: The risk is that something will upset the applecart and cause the abandonment of the planned action.
gold_claims.verification_note: bpl1957_p0003: terms verbatim in passage text; unit=qualitative statement.

gold_claims.claim: The ratio between general issues and work-outs moved from about 70-30 at the end of 1956 to about 85-15.
gold_claims.verification_note: bpl1957_p0003: terms verbatim in passage text; unit=figure.

gold_claims.claim: The market decline created greater opportunity among undervalued situations, so the portfolio was heavier in them than the year before.
gold_claims.verification_note: bpl1957_p0003: terms verbatim in passage text; unit=qualitative statement.

cases.verification_note: bpl1957_p0003 supply the 3 claims (upset the applecart; 70-30; greater opportunity).

cases.query: How did Buffett explain in his 1957 and 1960 letters that the partnership should do better in falling markets than in rising ones?

gold_claims.claim: In 1957 he said performance is likely to be better in a bear market than in a bull market, and in a substantial advance he would be well satisfied to match the Averages.
required_terms: better in a bear market than in a bull market
gold_claims.verification_note: bpl1957_p0009: terms verbatim in passage text; unit=qualitative statement.

gold_claims.claim: In 1960 he said results should be relatively better in moderately declining or static markets, though four years is entirely too short a period to be sure.
required_terms: relatively better in moderately declining or static markets
four years is entirely too short
gold_claims.verification_note: bpl1960_p0006: terms verbatim in passage text; unit=qualitative statement.

gold_claims.claim: In 1960 he said the important thing is to be beating par, since a four on a par three hole is not as good as a five on a par five hole.
gold_claims.verification_note: bpl1960_p0003: terms verbatim in passage text; unit=qualitative statement.

cases.verification_note: bpl1957_p0009, bpl1960_p0006, bpl1960_p0003 supply the 3 claims (better in a bear market than in a bull market; relatively better in moderately declining or static markets; beating par).
